subject: SLA measurement: telemetry handoff, regional weighting, and crediting methodology
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@pioneerhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA measurement: telemetry handoff, regional weighting, and crediting methodology

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the detailed questionnaire. Attached is our proposed evidence handoff and measurement boundary document (redwood-sla-evidence-matrix.pdf) plus a sample probe config you can review. I wanted to highlight three points up front that we hear commonly and that we've tried to capture in the matrix: 

1) Measurement source precedence: we treat customer-facing telemetry (your synthetic probes or client-observed success rates) as the primary source for crediting, with Redwood telemetry used for reconciliation when the customer telemetry is missing or inconsistent. Where both exist, we recommend a simple precedence rule (customer telemetry wins if it meets sanity checks) and an automated reconciliation report delivered weekly.

2) Regional aggregation and weighting: for customers operating multi-region deployments, we propose weighting by request volume per-region (not equal weighting across regions). This prevents small edge regions from disproportionately affecting global availability. The matrix includes an example calculation and a proposed minimum sample threshold.

3) Windowing and burst handling: our standard SLO window is 30 days with a 5-minute burst window for short spikes. For longer sustained degradations we use minute-by-minute telemetry aggregated into the 30-day window for credit triggers.

I've included proposed wording for contract language in the matrix (Section 3) and a working example for service-credit calculation. If you prefer, we can run the example against a recent 90-day slice of telemetry to show expected credits under both weighting models. 

Next steps: please confirm whether Pioneer intends to use internal synthetic probes (and if so, whether they will be routed through a primary region) or will rely on client-observed metrics. That determines which reconciliation path we prioritize.

Regards,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA measurement: telemetry handoff, regional weighting, and crediting methodology

Irene —

Thanks for this. A few clarifying points from Procurement/Platform: 

- Pioneer will run its own global synthetic probe network (we have three primary vantage clusters: us-west, us-east, eu-west). We expect to use our probes as the canonical measurement source for availability and latency SLOs.
- We want a consistent way to attribute cross-region failovers. If traffic shifts from us-west to us-east during an incident, we don't want to see credits triggered by the weight change alone.
- We need sample thresholds spelled out: what minimum probe coverage per-region is acceptable before Redwood uses Redwood telemetry for reconciliation?

Would you be able to provide the sample-threshold numbers and an example calculation showing: (a) equal-region weighting vs (b) volume-weighted approach for a multi-region service with uneven traffic? Procurement wants to include a worked example in the RFP response.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Infrastructure Procurement
Pioneer Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@pioneerhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA measurement: telemetry handoff, regional weighting, and crediting methodology

Samir —

Thanks for the quick feedback. I took the matrix and drafted a compact worked example (summary below) and included the explicit thresholds we've used in past enterprise contracts. I'll attach the CSV sample to the Drive link in the final deliverable. Key points: 

- Proposed per-region minimum probe coverage: 1 probe per 100k monthly requests or a minimum of 3 probes in that region, whichever is greater. If coverage is below that threshold for more than 7 consecutive days, Redwood will switch to the reconciliation mode using Redwood telemetry for that region until adequate coverage returns.

- Weighting example (simplified):
  * Regions: us-west (70% traffic), us-east (25%), eu-west (5%)
  * Equal weighting (3-region average) would treat each region as 33.3% regardless of traffic. If eu-west had a prolonged outage, credits would be larger under equal weighting than volume-weighted.
  * Volume-weighted calculation: availability = sum(region_availability * region_traffic_share). For the sample above: availability = A_usw*0.70 + A_use*0.25 + A_euw*0.05.

- Cross-region failover protection: we propose an incident-normalization clause that excludes traffic-weight shifts caused by automated regional failover if the failover is driven by a customer-side routing change (we ask customers to confirm routing events in the weekly incident report). For platform-initiated reroutes, we include traffic-shift normalization in the calculation so that credits are not double-counted.

- Service credit example: We proposed a 1% credit for availability falling between 99.5% and 99.0% (monthly), 5% for 99.0%–97.0%, and 15% below 97.0%. Credits are applied to the monthly invoice and calculated after weighting/normalization. The attached matrix shows how the calculation unfolds step-by-step for a sample 30-day window.

Irene/Marissa: can you confirm if Pioneer wants us to publish the reconciliation reports as a shared ledger (Drive link) or deliver them via an API push into their monitoring system? Pioneer, if you have a preference, we can adapt the report format.

Regards,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Reliability & Observability, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SLA measurement: telemetry handoff, regional weighting, and crediting methodology

Karthik/Irene —

This is helpful and closer to what we need. A few final items before we include this language in the RFP response: 

1) Please add the precise SQL-like pseudocode to compute the volume-weighted availability and the reconciliation rule (we prefer reproducible pseudocode we can run against our probe logs).
2) For the minimum probe coverage: the threshold looks reasonable, but can you shorten the reconciliation window from 7 days to 3 days? That will match our operational SLA with the edge vendor.
3) For the incident-normalization clause: Pioneer will accept platform-initiated normalization only if the platform (Redwood) provides a causal incident log (cause + timestamps + decision point) as part of the reconciliation report.

If you can confirm those three items we will accept the proposed weighting model and credit bands. Once confirmed, Procurement will sign off and push the finalized clauses into our contracting system.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Infrastructure Procurement
Pioneer Health
